# <span id="aanchor411"></span> <span id="aanchor412"></span> List Editor

FLOWCAL lists allow you to create logical groupings of like data points for meters, locations, and sources (such as grouping all meters in a given drilling basin, or all sources assigned to a given analyst). These lists can then be used to generate reports and exports, or to import, view, or edit data.

FLOWCAL supports static, dynamic and ordered lists. Static lists can only be edited through the List Editor, whereas dynamic lists are updated based on queries created in the Query Editor.

By default, static and dynamic lists are sorted by the object number (i.e., meter, location, or source number). Ordered lists display members in the order they were added. Typically, these are used for printing chart labels for gas meters in the order that the technician pulls charts.

<div class="procedure">

To access the List Editor: Go to **Setup** \> **List**.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 649;height: 513;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Static Ordered">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Creating Static or Ordered Lists</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Static Ordered">

<div class="procedure">

To create a static or ordered list from the List Editor:

1.  Go to **Setup** \> **List** to access the List Editor.

2.  Click the **List** button, and select "List" to create a list of meters and/or locations, or select "Source List" to create a list of sources.

3.  Click **New** and enter a name for the list. List names must be unique. They can be mixed case, and up to 50 characters.

4.  Select whether the list will be static or ordered.

    If you are creating an ordered list, the assets will display in the order they are selected.

5.  Populate the list. On the Lists tab under **Select from Available**, select members from the left side to add to the new list. To select more than one member, double-click a member, or hold the **Ctrl** key while clicking multiple items.

6.  Click the arrow buttons to add your selection(s) to the list.

    Click in the **Select from Available** grid or the **Selected** grid and press **Ctrl+F** to quickly search through the grid. You can also select **Search** from the menu.  

    To merge members from another list into the new list, select an existing list from the **Merge With** drop-down and click the **Merge** button.

    You can also copy a list of members from another program, such as Excel, if the members already exist in FLOWCAL. Right-click the grid and select **Paste** to add the items to the list.

    By default, items are displayed in order by number. Click a column header to sort data by that column.

7.  Click **Save**.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Dynamic">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Creating Dynamic Lists</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Dynamic">

<div class="procedure">

To create a dynamic list from the List Editor:

1.  Go to **Setup** \> **List** to access the List Editor.

2.  Click the **List** button, and select "List" to create a list of meters and/or locations, or select "Source List" to create a list of sources.

3.  Click **New** and enter a name for the list. List names must be unique. They can be mixed case, and up to 50 characters.

4.  Select **Dynamic** and choose a query from the **Query** drop-down to base the list on. The Selected grid will populate based on the query results.

    To create a new query, click the **Query** button or go to **Tools** \> **Query** to open the [Query Editor](../Tools/Query%20Editor.md). Once the query is created, click **OK** to return to the List Editor, and select the new query from the drop-down.

5.  To include or exclude specific members from a dynamic list, click the **Included** or **Excluded** tab as appropriate and use the arrow buttons to include or exclude available items from the list.

    Including or excluding query result members will not alter the query.

6.  Click **Save**.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Convert Dynamic">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Converting a Dynamic List to Static</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Convert Dynamic">

Use the merge function to quickly convert a dynamic list to a static list.

<div class="procedure">

To convert a dynamic list to a static list:

1.  Click the **Merge With** drop-down.
2.  Select a list and click the **Merge** button to compile members from the existing list into the new list.

All members from the list being merged will display in the grid under the list of selected locations, meters, or sources.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Deleting">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Deleting Lists</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Deleting">

Lists can only be deleted from the List Editor.

<div class="procedure">

To delete a list:

1.  Go to **Setup** \> **List** to open the List Editor.
2.  Click the **List** button to select list or source list.
3.  Select the list from the drop-down.
4.  Click the **Delete** button.

</div>

</div>
